newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Northern Tamil rebel town falls to Sri Lankan army.
newsitem.headline: Northern Tamil rebel town falls to Sri Lankan army.

text.p: Sri Lankan security forces have captured a northern town held by Tamil Tiger rebels after fierce air and artillery attacks, military officials said on Sunday.
The town of Nedunkeni, on the eastern flank of a three-pronged army push into guerrilla territory in the northern Wanni region, had been the scene of fierce fighting for three days.
"We have captured Nedunkeni," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters.
Further details of the offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) would be given later, he added.

Other military officials said at least four rebel camps had been destroyed and that some 100 guerrillas were believed killed in the battle for the town. There was no immediate word on army casualties in the latest fighting at Nedunkeni.

Two army divisions were on the move on separate axes trying to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, with Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north, military officials said.
The military now depends on costly and tenuous air and sea links to supply their bases and civilians in Jaffna.
A pitched battle was fought near Nedunkeni, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya, where troops advancing along the eastern flank were attacked by the rebels on Friday.
Heavy air and artillery attackes were launched on rebel reinforcements at Nedunkeni on Saturday.

The Defence Ministry has only said the main aim of the drive is to capture areas in the shrub-covered Wanni from the LTTE, who are waging a war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
Troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air cover, on Saturday secured the town of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya, after beating off a rebel counter-attack.
They are now pushing further north, heading towards the heavily fortified rebel-held town of Puliyankulam.
Civilians who fled Nedunkeni and arrived in Vavuniya said the army shelled rebel positions in the area for almost a week.
"There was heavy shell fire and fighting on Thursday," said Sangarapillai Selvaratnam, 43, a farmer. "Suddenly, the army marched into the town with tanks."
He was among 35 people, including women and children, brought by the army to Vavuniya on Friday.
Vavuniya government agent K. Ganesh said accommodation and cooked meals were being provided and that many more refugees were expected.
The LTTE's clandestine Voice of Tigers radio station, monitored by Reuters, said Nedunkeni was pounded by artillery and air force planes and many civilians had been displaced.
"Many civilians are living under trees," the radio said.
Military officials said 40 soldiers and more than 128 rebels had been killed in the fighting by Saturday. The LTTE say the army routinely exaggerates rebel casualties.
The military has been tight-lipped about where the troops are heading after breaking out of Vavuniya to launch the offensive, code-named "Jaya Sikuru," or "Sure of Victory", on Tuesday.
Hospital officials said more than 320 soldiers had been wounded.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
